content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli is an edible flower head of the plant Brassica oleracea var. italica, originally from the Mediterranean region. Raw broccoli has a slightly bitter, fresh taste and a crunchy texture. It is used in salads, smoothies, and as a side dish after brief cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli is rich in glucoraphanin, a compound that may support the body’s detoxification processes.
It is believed to have been first cultivated in ancient Rome before spreading worldwide.
Broccoli contains more vitamin C than an orange by about 100 %.
Broccoli seeds are used to produce oil high in omega‑3 fatty acids.
Broccoli belongs to the same family as cabbage, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts, and kale.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports immune function and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains sulforaphane
items.content: Sulforaphane is studied for its anti‑inflammatory and potential anti‑cancer properties.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of vitamins K and A
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, while vitamin A (as beta‑carotene) supports vision and skin health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Broccoli provides few calories, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Thyroid concerns
items.content: Raw cruciferous vegetables contain goitrogenic compounds that, in large amounts, may affect thyroid function.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergy to broccoli, resulting in skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: If stored above 4 °C for several days, broccoli can develop bacterial growth that may cause food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw broccoli florets can be eaten whole, sliced into bite‑size pieces, added to salads, blended into smoothies, or used as a dip with hummus. It can also be lightly marinated in lemon juice and olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store broccoli in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a small amount of moisture. Properly stored, it stays fresh for 3–5 days. Discard any yellowing or soft parts.
